greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who humbled himself for our sake, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you emptied yourself for love of us, Lord have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you invite us to the banquet of your kingdom, Christ have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the hope that endures beyond the grave, Lord have mercy.
psalm_response: I will praise you, Lord, in the assembly of your people.
homily:
We begin today with the image of a chair. Not an empty chair—though we all know the ache of that specific, hollow space—but a chair pulled up to a table. Think of the preparation that goes into a great dinner. The linens are smoothed, the plates are set, the invitation is sent, and the master of the house waits. There is a sense of anticipation in the air. The smell of the meal, the quiet clinking of glass, the expectation that the people you love are about to walk through the door. It is a scene of belonging. It is a scene of inclusion. Today, in the Gospel of Luke, we are invited to consider the guest list of God.

I want you to hold onto this image: the table. It is the place where we are known, where we are fed, and where we are gathered. It is the place where no one is left behind.

Let us speak the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who carry the light of Benjamin Vo in your souls: it has been four months since Ben crossed the threshold of this world into the next. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the coding, the aviation spotting, the simple joy of a shared meal—are suddenly interrupted by the sharp, cold realization that he is not there in the way he once was. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that feels far too heavy for human shoulders. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to be angry at the unfairness of a world that takes a boy of such brilliant promise. You are allowed to be human.

There is a temptation, when we carry this kind of sorrow, to look back at the path we walked and wonder if we missed a sign. We wonder if we could have seen something earlier, or done something differently, or if we failed in some hidden way. Let us lift that stone from your hearts right now. You missed nothing. You were the parents and the brother that Benjamin was given. You loved him with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of the world. You walked the globe with him, you shared the meals, you witnessed the brilliance of his mind and the gentleness of his spirit. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. Some sorrows in this fragile world arrive entirely beyond human reach, untouched by anything anyone did or failed to do. You are not to blame. Let that heavy stone fall to the ground; you are absolved. You were faithful. You were present. You were love in action.

Now, let the Gospel break in. The master of the house in the parable is not a distant, judgmental figure. He is a host whose heart is set on one thing: that his home be filled. When those who were first invited make their excuses—the field, the oxen, the marriage—the master does not despair. He turns to the streets, the alleys, the highways, and the hedgerows. He says, ‘Make them come in.’ He is relentless in his mercy. He is determined that the table will not be empty. This is the heart of God. He is not a God who keeps a ledger of who 'deserves' to be there. He is a God who goes to the edges of the earth to find the ones he loves.

Benjamin was a boy who understood this kind of openness. Think of his brilliant, searching mind—the way he mastered mathematics and cloud infrastructure, the way he built games and dreamed of ‘con chim airlines.’ But think even more of his heart. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William, who was suffering from strokes. He didn't need to break it open, he didn't need to empty it; the offer itself was the revelation of his character. It was the movement of a soul that already understood that we are here to give, not to hoard. That is the boy you raised. That is the boy who is now at the banquet of heaven, interceding for you. He is not a memory; he is a living soul, fully alive in the love of God. He is a guest who has already taken his seat, and he is waiting for the rest of his family to arrive.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess.

We hear in the letter to the Philippians today: ‘Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God something to be grasped. Rather, he emptied himself.’ This is the mystery of our faith. The God of the universe did not grasp at his own glory; he let it go to become a slave, to become human, to suffer, and to die. He did this so that he could be with us in our suffering. He did this so that when we walk through the valley of the shadow of death, we do not walk alone. He has been there. He has felt the weight of the cross. He is the one who holds Benjamin now, and he is the one who holds you.

There is a peace that comes from knowing that we are held. It is not a peace that takes away the pain, but it is a peace that keeps us from being destroyed by it. It is the peace of knowing that Benjamin is waiting. He is waiting in the light, he is waiting in the place where there is no more struggling, no more darkness, only the clear, bright presence of the Father. He is waiting for you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is the sign that the work is going well. That smile is the promise that the reunion is certain.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin smiling at you from the other side. Let yourself be gathered. Trust that you are held. And walk out into the world with the quiet, unshakeable hope that the love you share is the most powerful force in the universe. It is stronger than death. It is more enduring than time. And it is the very thing that will bring you home to each other. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may his face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may he give you his peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's presence, we pray to the Lord.
For all who carry the heavy cross of grief, that they may be consoled by the promise of the Resurrection and find strength in the love of God, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
Have among yourselves the same attitude 
that is also yours in Christ Jesus,
Who, though he was in the form of God,
did not regard equality with God
something to be grasped.
Rather, he emptied himself,
taking the form of a slave,
coming in human likeness;
and, found human in appearance,
he humbled himself,
becoming obedient to death,
even death on a cross.
Because of this, God greatly exalted him
and bestowed on him the name
that is above every name,
that at the name of Jesus
every knee should bend,
of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue confess that
Jesus Christ is Lord,
to the glory of God the Father.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (26a) I will praise you, Lord, in the assembly of your people.
I will fulfill my vows before those who fear him.
The lowly shall eat their fill;    
they who seek the LORD shall praise him:
“May your hearts be ever merry!”
R. I will praise you, Lord, in the assembly of your people.
All the ends of the earth
shall remember and turn to the LORD;
All the families of the nations
shall bow down before him.
R. I will praise you, Lord, in the assembly of your people. 
For dominion is the LORD’s,
 and he rules the nations.
To him alone shall bow down
all who sleep in the earth.
R. I will praise you, Lord, in the assembly of your people.
To him my soul shall live;
my descendants shall serve him.
Let the coming generation be told of the LORD
that they may proclaim to a people yet to be born
the justice he has shown.
R.  I will praise you, Lord, in the assembly of your people.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
One of those at table with Jesus said to him,
“Blessed is the one who will dine in the Kingdom of God.”
He replied to him,
“A man gave a great dinner to which he invited many.
When the time for the dinner came,
he dispatched his servant to say to those invited,
‘Come, everything is now ready.’
But one by one, they all began to excuse themselves.
The first said to him,
‘I have purchased a field and must go to examine it;
I ask you, consider me excused.’
And another said, ‘I have purchased five yoke of oxen
and am on my way to evaluate them;
I ask you, consider me excused.’
And another said, ‘I have just married a woman,
and therefore I cannot come.’
The servant went and reported this to his master.
Then the master of the house in a rage commanded his servant,
‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the town
and bring in here the poor and the crippled, the blind and the lame.’
The servant reported, ‘Sir, your orders have been carried out
and still there is room.’
The master then ordered the servant,
‘Go out to the highways and hedgerows
and make people come in that my home may be filled.
For, I tell you, none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.’”

pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
